args.value: The week 2026-08-04..2026-08-10 largest apparent BOD price-order inversion
The apparent price-order inversion selected by the pre-declared procedure in investigations/001-largest-apparent-inversion can be fully explained from publicly available information.

EXPLAINED: the selected apparent inversion (2026-08-06 SP29, bid; T_LARYW-1 accepted at -179.76 GBP/MWh vs E_RHEI-1 unaccepted at +9949 GBP/MWh) is fully accounted for by zero deliverable bid volume on the unaccepted side (FPN=0, MELS=0, demand capacity 0). The null hypothesis survives. SO-flagged acceptance documents a system-driven curtailment.
Method Study 001: phantom liquidity in GB BM data (retrospective, corpus 2026-08-04..10)

In the 2026-08-04..2026-08-10 corpus, more than half of raw pairwise price-order inversions involve an unaccepted alternative that is clearly non-deliverable under the conservative public physical-state bound declared in METHOD-STUDY-001.md.

CONFIRMED: 67.3 percent of the 3,856,031 raw pairwise price-order inversions in the 2026-08-04..10 corpus (2,595,381) involve an alternative provably non-deliverable under the pre-declared conservative public physical-state bound; these collapse to 76,289 of 158,953 unique alternatives (48.0 percent). The residual (1,260,650 pairwise; 82,664 unique) SURVIVES the checks applied and is not thereby evidence of dispatch error.
Method Study 001B: the naive opportunity screen vs physical state and NESO skip methodology (retrospective, corpus 2026-08-04..10)

For the majority of accepted actions in the 2026-08-04..2026-08-10 corpus that have at least one apparent better-priced alternative under the Investigation 001 BOD-only rule, the naive screen's single top-ranked alternative is provably non-deliverable under Method Study 001's conservative physical-state bound.

CONFIRMED: 64.5 percent (16,336 of 25,326) of accepted actions' naive top-ranked alternatives were provably non-deliverable. The naive screen's head is entirely phantom-led: all of the top 10/100/1000 by gap and by notional had a non-deliverable number-one pick; raw-vs-feasibility-aware top-100 overlap is zero. The naive counterfactual notional (arithmetic on public numbers, not value) fell 90.5 percent (GBP 607.8m to 57.6m). Against NESO's official skip methodology (6,390 cells, full window coverage): agreement 34.9 to 64.7 percent after the single physical test, catching 1,988 of 2,017 NESO skips; top-20 disagreements are NESO's own documented Wind offer and Behind constraint exclusions. Spearman vs skipped volumes 0.34 to 0.39: magnitudes remain untracked.
Method Study 001C: anatomy of the 2,226 post-filter disagreements with NESO skip methodology (retrospective, corpus 2026-08-04..10)

The majority of the 2,226 cells flagged by the feasibility-aware screen but not skipped at NESO stage 5 are attributable to NESO-published exclusion categories or to full acceptance of the in-merit volume, leaving a minority unmatched by public operational explanations.

CONFIRMED, far beyond the majority threshold: of the 2,226 post-filter disagreement cells, 99.7 percent carry a public operational explanation - 40.3 percent absent from NESO's in-merit availability universe, 34.5 percent behind constraint, 23.1 percent other published exclusion categories or full acceptance - leaving 6 cells (0.27 percent, all bid-side battery/small units) unmatched. Layered agreement with NESO stage 5 on the fixed 6,390-cell universe: 34.9 percent naive, 64.7 percent with physical deliverability, 66.6 percent peak adding wind-offer exclusions; binary adoption of volumetric exclusion categories beyond that degrades agreement (constraint layer forfeits 970 genuine catches), so further progress requires volume-level reconstruction.
Method Study 001D: explanation-testing of the six unmatched unit-day cells (retrospective, corpus 2026-08-04..10)
Each of the six unmatched unit-day cells identified by Method Study 001C can be fully explained from public period-level information.

CONFIRMED - all six explained by one mechanism: every cell's gap-generating accepted counterparts are dominated by actions NESO excludes from its accepted-side skip-comparison stack (Behind constraint 760..43,752 rows per cell-date, plus System-tagged), corroborated by SO-flagged acceptances in the exact qualifying periods (constraint management on Seagreen/Viking/Edinbane wind, Cruachan/Sloy hydro, Grain CCGT). Our screen made a comparison NESO's methodology declines to make, so no skip is recorded. Deliverable-headroom bounds (0-7 MW for BHOLB-1) and daily-vs-period granularity contribute context; battery state of charge was not needed. The corpus week's unmatched residue is now zero; lesson for 002+: attribution must key operator exclusions on BOTH sides of every comparison.
BESS Study 001: benchmark fragility under GC0166 duration-aware data (method study, corpus 2026-07-01..31)

For the July 2026 GC0166 early-submitter panel, less than half of the price-only apparent BM opportunity survives to the public-as-of duration-aware rung, under the rules declared in METHOD-STUDY-BESS-001.md.
neso-data-portal July skip rates via evidence/neso-july-manifest.json
elexon-insights July panel physical via evidence/physical-july-manifest.json

CONFIRMED, far beyond threshold: for the July 2026 GC0166 early-submitter panel (4 units, mechanically selected at 1488/1488 coverage; 2 candidates excluded by the pre-declared 80 percent gate), pooled apparent BM opportunity of GBP 618,908,576 at the price-only rung retains 4.72 percent (GBP 29,215,605) after physical headroom, 2.61 percent (GBP 16,133,648) under hindsight duration envelopes, and 2.40 percent (GBP 14,870,059) using only information publicly observable by the decision cutoff (period start minus 60 minutes). GBP 1,263,589 of the duration-aware figure, 7.8 percent, was feasible only with information published after the cutoff (989 unit-direction-periods). At the operational-context rung GBP 295,915 (0.05 percent) carries no NESO exclusion context on either side; the context split is a disclosure, not a verdict. All figures are arithmetic on public numbers, never achievable value; unknown buckets: 2 periods. Duration-awareness alone removed 44.8 percent of what physics permitted - the first quantified measure of what GC0166 data adds to counterfactual credibility.

CORRECTION of fnd-bess-001-fragility (which remains on the record as published): the GBP 1,263,589 point-in-time figure was a pooled NET difference concealing revisions in both directions. Period-level decomposition: final-vintage MDO/MDB supported GBP 4,689,718 of opportunity not publicly supportable at the decision cutoff (989 unit-direction-periods) AND removed GBP 3,426,133 that the contemporaneous public envelope had supported (1,991 unit-direction-periods); net GBP 1,263,584 (the GBP 5 residue is two unknown-at-R3p periods). A hindsight benchmark does not merely know more - it reconstructs a materially different feasible state from the one publicly observable at decision time, in either direction. All other figures of the original finding are unchanged and reconfirmed (rung totals byte-identical on re-run); the timeliness claim is corrected to: July 2026 is the first full month for which the new public MDO/MDB data exists. Figures are arithmetic on public numbers, never achievable value.
Investigation 003: Follow the Constraint - reconstruct the highest-RRT-score congestion episode of May 2026

The full sequence of publicly observable actions in the episode selected by the pre-declared rule (highest re-trade-cycle score, May 2026) can be reconstructed and its realised cashflows accounted for from public data, with each apparently perverse step explained by the incentives and constraints visible at the time.
elexon-insights May 2026 corpus via evidence/may-manifest.json (companions: neso-may, pn-may, ebocf-may manifests in same evidence dir)

PARTLY CONFIRMED, with the observability boundary precisely mapped. The frozen rule selected constraint group SSE-SP, 2026-05-18..31 (right-censored by the window): 8,259 repeat-curtailment cycles consistent with RRT, 69,869 MWh storage bid-down. The observable sequence reconstructs at scale (excerpt day 2026-05-20: 1,060 cycles; focus unit E_DOLLB-1: 21 cycles, 88 distinct acceptances in one day, repeatedly instructed from scheduled export through zero to around -99 MW import, NONE SO-flagged in the public record). Published money accounts to Elexon's own indicative figures (episode dates, GB-wide scope: storage bids -6,736,338 GBP, storage offers +9,152,108, non-storage offers +78,392,272; SSE-SP published outturn constraint cost 11,510,565 GBP). Two links are NOT publicly observable and are the finding: (1) the intraday re-sale that turns repetition into re-trading; (2) the unit-to-constraint-group mapping that would localise money to the boundary. No figure is a cost of RRT; concurrency is observed, substitution never asserted.

ofgem Repetitive Re-trading (RRT) by electricity storage in transmission constraint periods, policy paper, June 2026; pinned at data/raw/ofgem/repetitive-re-trading-policy-paper-2026-06.pdf via evidence/reference-manifest.json

CORRECTION AND STRENGTHENING of fnd-003-episode-reconstructed (which remains on the record as published). (1) Attribution: the frozen selection rule scores an episode by counting repeat-curtailment cycles across the entire declared GB storage universe over the episode dates; no constraint-group filter was declared and none is publicly implementable - the missing unit-to-group mapping the original finding itself identified. The 8,259 cycles and 69,869 MWh are GB-wide storage activity concurrent with the SSE-SP episode dates and must not be presented as activity behind SSE-SP. (2) Methodology alignment, from the pinned Ofgem RRT policy paper (June 2026, art-003-ofgem-rrt-paper): NESO estimates the balancing cost impact of RRT from storage at approximately GBP 99m in FY 2025/26 (12-hour search window), up from approximately GBP 64m in FY 2024/25, with pumped storage around 80 percent of the two-year total; the methodology counts only settlement periods with a positive FPN, a SYSTEM-FLAGGED bid acceptance, and a subsequent net-upward PN revision within a 3/6/12-hour horizon - computed from timestamped PN revision history that is not public (only final PN vintages are). (3) Descriptive tally over the episode dates (evidence: so-flag-tally.json): 90,020 distinct storage-unit acceptances GB-wide, of which 2,904 (3.2 percent) are SO-flagged; focus unit E_DOLLB-1 recorded 1,492 acceptances with zero SO-flagged, so its 21 excerpt-day cycles cannot be presented as a demonstrated constraint-driven RRT example. Consequence: the repeat-curtailment score is a concurrence signature, not NESO's RRT count, and the public record cannot reproduce NESO's RRT diagnosis - the missing inputs are point-in-time PN revision history and authoritative constraint attribution.

Mystery 002 - what survives a hardened selector on an untouched week
The apparent price-order inversion selected by this hardened, pre-declared procedure can be fully explained from publicly available information.

EXPLAINED. The frozen hardened rule selected 2026-08-12 period 33 offer: T_SEAB-1 accepted at GBP890.00/MWh (0.125 MWh) while C__PSTAT011 was unaccepted at GBP0.00/MWh. NESO's own published skip-rate data excludes BOTH sides from its merit stack - the alternative as a Wind offer, the accepted action as System-tagged - so the null hypothesis survives. Methodological finding: Amendment B screened on Elexon soFlag, which acceptance 176767 does not carry, while NESO classifies the same unit's offer as System-tagged; the two signals differ and soFlag is the weaker. Amendment A admitted the alternative on MEL-FPN>0, but a wind MEL is a forecast, not firm capability. Amendment A alone still removed 74 percent of candidates and 70 percent of naive notional on a week it never saw.
elexon-insights 2026-06-24 settlement day + context (EBOCF, B1610, FUELINST, SYSWARN) via investigations/004-most-expensive-half-hour/evidence/day-manifest.json and context-manifest.json

The half-hour's publicly observable state can be reconstructed coherently from public data, and every major action in it is consistent with the visible system context, without requiring non-public information to explain at the level of mechanism. Where the published Constraints total cannot be decomposed from public data, that gap is itself a declared finding.

PARTLY EXPLAINED, with the observability boundary where the declaration predicted it. The frozen rule selected 2026-06-24 p42 (Constraints GBP1,176,150), which falls inside the 19:00-22:00 window NESO had warned about the previous night and CANCELLED at 13:20; all four of June's dearest half-hours fall inside it. NESO's own notice supplies the bridge: 1,250-1,300 MW of generation was excluded from available system margin BY SYSTEM CONSTRAINTS, against a 1,450-1,900 MW shortfall. At the window's open the dispatchable fleet was at published limits (CCGT headroom 88 MW; pumped storage, nuclear and non-pumped hydro zero). Through the peak the record shows 1,085 MWh of accepted bids across 113 units with ZERO accepted offers, pumped storage held at 0 against a 150 MW schedule, and the large positive money OUTSIDE the BM (GBP1,277,241 over 1,173 MWh, all classified Energy) while BM cashflow is negative. Not determinable from public data: why the Constraints series peaks in p42 rather than p41 where BSAD peaks; the Peterhead gap between ~729 MW metered and ~1,150 MW instructed; and whether the generation NESO excluded from margin is the generation visible being bid down. No transmission boundary is named.
